description: Canonical Nuxel capability registry. Single source of truth for what a capability means, what mechanism actually enforces it on the target device, and which attacker-privilege class that enforcement holds against. Consumed by nuxel-permd.py, nuxel-permissions (GTK), tools/s10plus/a33/verify-permissions.py and the security auditor. Never state a stronger guarantee than the 'enforceable'/'limitation' fields below.

target.kernel_config_source: /proc/config.gz on the handset (readable; recorded in A29/A32 records). Cgroup prerequisites verified in the A16/A17 .config: CONFIG_CGROUPS=y CONFIG_MEMCG=y CONFIG_CGROUP_SCHED=y CONFIG_CGROUP_PIDS=y CONFIG_CGROUP_FREEZER=y CONFIG_CPUSETS=y CONFIG_CGROUP_DEVICE=y CONFIG_CGROUP_CPUACCT=y CONFIG_CGROUP_BPF=y CONFIG_NAMESPACES=y; CONFIG_BPF_LSM is unset.
kernel_facts_measured: kauditd is running -> the audit subsystem is enabled in the vendor kernel
CONFIG_BPF_LSM is not set -> 'bpf-restrict-fs: BPF LSM hook not enabled' (systemd warning)
Landlock is mainline >= 5.13; it cannot exist in a 4.14 tree. /proc/sys/kernel/landlock/abi_version is absent.
nftables 'socket cgroupv2' matching is mainline >= 5.13. On 4.14 the per-app network match must use cgroup v1 net_cls classid (nft 'meta cgroup <classid>').
Kernel lockdown LSM is mainline >= 4.17 -> not present.
Kernel CFI / arm64 Shadow Call Stack (>= 5.7), BTI and Pointer Authentication (>= 5.9/ARMv8.3+) are absent; Exynos 9820 is ARMv8.2-A so PAuth/BTI are also absent in hardware.

enforcement_baseline.unprivileged_app: DAC (file ownership/mode) + per-asset wrapper (portal) + AppArmor IF the vendor kernel has the AppArmor LSM enabled (must be read from /sys/kernel/security/lsm on the handset; not assumed).
enforcement_baseline.root: Nothing in this document constrains uid 0 / CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Root compromise is explicitly out of scope for every claim here.

portal.title: D-Bus portal gate (org.nuxel.Portal)
portal.honest_note: The portal is a userspace broker. It refuses the request when no grant exists and logs the decision. An app that never calls the portal is not blocked by it.

sandbox-profile.title: Per-app sandbox profile (cgroup + namespace + seccomp + nftables classid)
sandbox-profile.honest_note: Layers that the 4.14 kernel actually provides: namespaces, seccomp BPF, cgroup limits, cgroup v1 net_cls network matching. Landlock is unavailable.

apparmor.title: AppArmor MAC label (/etc/apparmor.d/*)
apparmor.honest_note: Profiles ship in the repository, but they only take effect if the vendor 4.14 kernel has CONFIG_SECURITY_APPARMOR=y and apparmor is in /sys/kernel/security/lsm. Verify with tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-security-audit.sh before claiming enforcement. If absent, the profiles are inert and must be labelled as such.

nftables.title: nftables ruleset (configs/nftables/)
nftables.honest_note: Per-app matching on this kernel uses net_cls classid. A process outside the matched cgroup (or root) is not constrained by these rules.

file-mode.title: POSIX file ownership and mode (DAC)
file-mode.honest_note: DAC is the only filesystem boundary left on 4.14 once Landlock is unavailable. It cannot express per-app path allow-lists.

systemd-cgroup.title: systemd unit confinement (cgroup v2, MemoryMax/TasksMax/DeviceAllow)
systemd-cgroup.honest_note: cgroup v2 works on 4.14. DeviceAllow needs the BPF device controller, which this kernel lacks (CONFIG_BPF_LSM unset) -> systemd warns and proceeds without device ACLs.

none.title: No enforcement implemented
none.honest_note: Labelled NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE / documented limitation. No cosmetic switch is exposed for these.

not-applicable.title: Not applicable (no sensitive resource)
not-applicable.honest_note: The capability names a UI affordance, not a protected resource.

capabilities.title: Audio playback
capabilities.description: Play sound through the speaker or headphones
capabilities.limitation: Audio OUTPUT is not a protected resource: playing sound discloses nothing, so there is no privacy gate and none is faked. The only boundary is DAC on /dev/snd/*. The S10+ speaker path itself (beyond-madera / CS47L93 / CS35L40 / ABox, low volume only) is unverified - see manual proof 06-audio.

capabilities.title: Background execution
capabilities.description: Keep running after the UI is closed
capabilities.limitation: Enforced by systemd (cgroup v2: MemoryMax/TasksMax). cgroup v2 works on 4.14 but the BPF device controller does not (CONFIG_BPF_LSM unset), so DeviceAllow is not applied (systemd warns and proceeds).

capabilities.title: Bluetooth
capabilities.description: Scan, pair and talk to Bluetooth devices
capabilities.limitation: Enforced by D-Bus policy on org.bluez plus group ownership of the BlueZ socket. Bluetooth hardware itself is unverified on the S10+ (manual proof 11-bluetooth).

capabilities.title: Calendar
capabilities.limitation: Same DAC/portal story as contacts; no path-level kernel confinement on 4.14.

capabilities.title: Phone calls
capabilities.limitation: Same as sms: D-Bus/portal mediation only; the Shannon modem is not integrated upstream, so no call can actually be placed yet.

capabilities.title: Camera
capabilities.description: Capture photos and preview the camera feed
capabilities.limitation: Device-node access is gated by DAC (/dev/video* mode/group) and by AppArmor only if the vendor 4.14 kernel enables that LSM. Landlock (which would give per-app path/device confinement) does not exist on 4.14, so an unprivileged app that can open /dev/video* is not stopped by the permission store.
capabilities.test: tools/s10plus/a33/verify-permissions.py --app pwa/nuxel-apps/camera-gallery; manual: deny grant, observe portal refusal in journalctl -u nuxel-portal

capabilities.title: Clipboard
capabilities.description: Read and write the shared clipboard
capabilities.limitation: Clipboard mediation needs a Wayland compositor data-device. This kernel has no DRM/KMS (# CONFIG_DRM is not set), so Phoc runs headless only and there is no system-wide clipboard to mediate. Labelled NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE; no switch is exposed.

capabilities.title: Clock and alarms
capabilities.description: Read the system clock and manage alarms/timers
capabilities.limitation: Reading the system clock and setting alarms is not a protected resource; there is nothing to enforce, so no switch is exposed. Listed so that manifests declaring clock:status resolve instead of being reported as unknown. Time/RTC persistence itself is owned by manual proof 05-timekeeping.

capabilities.title: Contacts
capabilities.description: Read and write the contacts database
capabilities.limitation: The contacts store is a file owned by the nuxel-contacts uid; other apps are stopped by DAC, not by a per-app kernel rule. Portal mediation covers Evolution/EDS D-Bus access.

capabilities.title: Display ownership
capabilities.description: Take ownership of the framebuffer for full-screen rendering
capabilities.limitation: Single framebuffer owner is a repository-level protocol (receipt-driven handoff), not a kernel permission. /dev/fb0 is crw------- root:root, so only the owning process (or root) can render. Correct, but not a per-app capability the kernel mediates.

capabilities.title: Location
capabilities.limitation: No GNSS bring-up on the S10+ yet (see manual proof 13-gps) -> the data path is BLOCKED_HARDWARE; the grant gate is implemented and refusal is enforced by the portal only.

capabilities.title: Microphone
capabilities.limitation: ALSA/PipeWire capture access is DAC-gated (/dev/snd/*). The portal gate is a userspace broker; a recorder that bypasses the portal is only stopped by DAC/AppArmor. The S10+ capture path itself is NOT yet verified (see manual proof 06-audio).

capabilities.title: Network access
capabilities.description: Open outbound and inbound network connections
capabilities.limitation: On 4.14 the per-app path is cgroup v1 net_cls classid matching (nft 'meta cgroup 0x...'). The cgroupv2 'socket cgroupv2' matcher used by the newer ruleset needs Linux >= 5.13 and is BLOCKED_KERNEL here. Processes that leave the matched cgroup, and root, are not constrained.
capabilities.test: tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-firewall.sh console-verify; nft list ruleset (live group applies rules)

capabilities.title: Notifications
capabilities.limitation: Rate-limited by the notification service; there is no protected resource to enforce against, so this is a policy affordance, not a security boundary.

capabilities.title: Phone status
capabilities.description: Read signal strength, network registration and SIM identity
capabilities.limitation: Read-only metadata via the bridge/portal. No modem -> returns an honest 'no modem' state rather than fabricated values.

capabilities.title: SMS
capabilities.limitation: ModemManager D-Bus access is mediated by AppArmor (if enabled) and by the portal; the modem itself is not yet up on the S10+ (Shannon, no upstream plugin) -> radio path is BLOCKED_FIRMWARE/BLOCKED_HARDWARE.

capabilities.title: (reserved) raw modem commands
capabilities.description: Reserved capability for direct modem AT access; intentionally unimplemented
capabilities.limitation: Deliberately NOT supported: raw modem access would bypass every portal rule. Declared here so a manifest that asks for it is reported as an unsupported capability instead of being silently ignored.

capabilities.title: Files and storage
capabilities.description: Read and write the app's own data directory (and files the user hands over)
capabilities.limitation: App data lives in /var/app/<app-id>/data owned by a dedicated uid (DAC). Without Landlock there is no path-level allow-list, so 'the app may read only these paths' is not kernel-enforced on 4.14.

capabilities.title: USB devices
capabilities.limitation: Mediated by the portal and DAC only. Note the live-console CDC-ACM gadget interface is deliberately reserved for the owner console and is never granted to apps.
